application_guidance.input_pattern: A same-sample smooth directional estimator with known direction moments.
read_original_when: Changing noise coupling, direction law or differentiability domain.
Using conditional moments in an adaptive process.

issues: The intermediate error vector in §4.2 may depend on x; no independence of that vector from x is asserted.
evidence.statement_check: Visually checked Eqs.(9)–(10) on pp.5–6, their standing context on pp.2,4–5 and complete source Proof p.15.

content.intended_use: Bound estimator bias and second moment.

map: Convexity and the smooth upper bound give r_X(Z)=[F(θ+hZ;X)−F(θ;X)]/h−<g(θ;X),Z>, with 0≤r_X(Z)≤hL(X)||Z||²/2, as in Eq.(24).

Write H=<g,Z>Z+r_X(Z)Z. Independence and isotropy give E[<g,Z>Z]=E g=∇f. The remaining expectation has norm at most (h/2)E L(X) E[||Z||²||Z||_*]≤(hL_P/2)E[||Z||²||Z||_*], proving Eq.(9). If L_P=0 the remainder vanishes and v can be zero.

Using ||a+b||_*²≤2||a||_*²+2||b||_*² gives E||H||_*²≤2E||<g,Z>Z||_*²+(h²/2)E[L(X)²||Z||^4||Z||_*²]. Assumption D conditional on X bounds the first term by 2s(d)E||g||_*²; independence factors the second into (h²/2)L_P²M², proving Eq.(10).
proofs.omitted_details: Complete paraphrase of the actually read source argument, not a new local Theorem or independent Reviewer certificate. The source suppresses sample dependence in its intermediate v; the remainder notation above makes that dependence explicit.
proofs.reading_coverage: Viewed pp.4–6 for setup and statement and all of §4.2 on p.15 for the source argument.

assumptions: Standing convex differentiable sample-function setting of pp.2,4–5; queried segments are in the smooth domain so Eq.(5) and its Taylor remainder are defined.
The measurable gradient satisfies E g(θ;X)=∇f(θ) and E||g(θ;X)||_*²<∞. No uniform G bound or MD geometry is needed for this pointwise conclusion.
X,Z are independent; E ZZ^T=I_d; M<∞; for every a∈R^d, E||<a,Z>Z||_*²≤s(d)||a||_*² (Assumption D and standing isotropy).
For P-almost every x the sample gradient is L(x)-Lipschitz in the stated primal/dual norms, with L_P<∞ (Assumption E).
statement.objects_and_definitions: Fix θ∈Θ and h>0. Let X∼P and Z∼μ be independent, H=[F(θ+hZ;X)−F(θ;X)]Z/h, g(θ;X)=∇F(θ;X), f=E F, and ||·||_* the dual norm. Define M=(E||Z||^4||Z||_*²)^(1/2), L_P=(E L(X)²)^(1/2). Here h denotes the source's u.
statement.parameter_domains: d≥1 integer; h>0; finite s(d)>0, M,L_P≥0 and the stated moments. No Bregman radius, minimizer, step size or prox operation is required.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every fixed θ and every legal h>0 satisfying the conditions, expectations are over independent X,Z. There exists v=v(θ,h)∈R^d with the stated norm bound. No adaptive-trajectory claim is made.

checked_locators: pp.4–6 Eq.(5), Assumptions D–E, Lemma 1 Eqs.(9)–(10)
use_restrictions: Staging proposal only; no independent Reviewer or publication is claimed.
Pointwise estimator result only; no optimization rate, prox requirement or unrestricted Oracle Complexity claim.

title: Bias and second moment of the smooth paired directional estimator
use_when: Check a same-sample smooth directional estimator before a separate optimization analysis.
